ready1_open_rewrite.title: GeoSQA Open-ended Question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Read the figure on the right. It is known that place N sees sunset earlier than place P; at this moment, within the 70° latitude line in the figure there is polar day, and after another 8h, the solar altitude at place N reaches the maximum of that day. <image1> At this moment, the place where the solar altitude angle is the greatest may be located in an area affected by what type of ocean current?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: An area through which a warm current flows

matched_variant_raw.expected_answer: An area through which a warm current flows

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Read the figure on the right. It is known that place N sees sunset earlier than place P; at this moment, within the 70° latitude line in the figure there is polar day, and after another 8h, the solar altitude at place N reaches the maximum of that day. <image1> At this moment, the place where the solar altitude angle is the greatest may be located in an area affected by what type of ocean current?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: An area through which a warm current flows
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure on the right is a schematic diagram of a latitude-longitude graticule. The upper right corner is the convergence point of multiple straight meridians, and the curved lines represent parallels; labels such as 30° and 60° can be seen in the figure. N and P are located on nearby parallel arcs on the left side of the figure, and N is above P. Then reason: the place where the solar altitude angle is greatest is the subsolar point at this moment. The question stem says that within the 70° latitude line in the figure there is polar day, indicating that the boundary of polar day is at the 70° latitude line, so the subsolar latitude is 90°-70°=20°, and it is in the hemisphere where the polar day shown in the figure is located. After another 8h, the solar altitude at place N reaches the maximum of that day, that is, place N will reach local time 12 o'clock after another 8 hours, so at this moment the local time at place N is 4 o'clock; the local time on the meridian where the subsolar point is located is 12 o'clock, differing from place N by 8×15°=120°, that is, the subsolar-point meridian is 120° east of place N. Also because place N sees sunset earlier than place P, it can be determined that place N is farther east than place P, and based on this the direction in which longitude increases or decreases in the figure and the hemisphere position are determined. Matching the 20° latitude line with the corresponding meridian to the world distribution of ocean currents, it can be known that this subsolar point may fall in a low-latitude sea area affected by a warm current.
